question: What is different about castor seeds?

options.text: It is the only rabi crop
It is neither rabi nor kharif
It is both rabi and kharif crop

solution:
The correct answer is It is __**both rabi and kharif crop.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• ** Castor seeds are a unique crop as they can be grown in both rabi and kharif seasons.**
 
• This means that farmers have the flexibility to cultivate** castor seeds twice a year.**
 
• Castor seeds are also known as non-food oilseed crops.
 
• They are primarily grown for their oil, which is used in a variety of industries such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and lubricants.
 
• Castor seeds require **warm temperatures and well-drained soil to grow.**
 
• They are not suitable for areas with **heavy rainfall or high humidity.**
 
• Castor seeds are also known for their high resistance to pests and diseases. This makes them a low-maintenance crop, which is ideal for small farmers who may not have access to expensive pesticides.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Rabi crops are those that are sown in the winter and harvested in the spring. Examples of rabi crops include wheat, barley, and mustard.
 
• Kharif crops are those that are sown in the rainy season and harvested in the autumn. Examples of Kharif crops include rice, maize, and cotton.
 
• Zaid crops are those that are grown in the summer season between rabi and kharif. Examples of zaid crops include watermelon, cucumber, and bitter gourd.
